text:
maya: Heads-up: we're seeing a p99 tail spike (~+30ms) on canary after the kernel-picker change last night for redwood/open-13b-v1 (seq=1024). p95 looks unchanged.
chris: Confirmed on 3/3 canary hosts. p50/p95 steady, p99 moved from ~220ms -> ~250ms.
maya: I grabbed flamegraphs and a few KV cache traces. Main anomaly is a long scheduling wait in the continuous-batcher path, not pure kernel execution.
olga: Hmm, scheduling wait -> could be microbatches not coalescing because max_wait_ms was lowered in that deploy? We changed it from 18 -> 8ms in scheduler PR #4123.
jiang: Yes PR note said reduce max_wait_ms to help latency for small requests. But that reduces batching for medium-sized traffic which hurts throughput and increases kernel-switch overhead.
chris: Profiling snapshot: many tiny dispatches hitting the fused kernel selector, which then does a cold path kernel swap and a KV cache handshake. The swap adds ~8-12ms occasionally when batch tokens < 512.
maya: Exact trace snippet (sanitized):
```
scheduler.cc: enqueue_wait() +9.8ms
kernel_picker.cpp: pick_kernel() +3.2ms
fallback_mux: kernel_switch() +11.4ms
kv_cache.cpp: maybe_warm_kv() +6.1ms
```
chris: So two interacting things: (1) smaller microbatches -> more frequent kernel switching, (2) KV cache initialization for those microbatches that miss. Combined they blow up the tail even if avg exec time is fine.
olga: Potential quick experiments: A) increase max_wait_ms back toward 16-20ms so we get more coalescing, B) bump max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 4096 to reduce kernel_switch frequency, C) add a tiny hysteresis that avoids kernel-switch for batches < 256 tokens.
jiang: Agreed. Also worth measuring KV hit rate distribution by request size. If small requests are cache-miss heavy, any decrease in batching will make misses surface more often.
chris: I ran a micro experiment on a single host: set max_wait_ms=20 and max_batch_tokens=4096 for 1 hour. Result: p99 dropped ~18ms (not fully back but much better), p95 unchanged, throughput +4%. KV hit-rate improved by ~6% for short requests.
maya: Nice. But raising max_wait_ms increases median latency slightly for ultra-low-latency clients. We need to quantify SLO impact across slices.
olga: Suggest A/B canary: route 10% traffic for 24h with two variants: (1) max_wait_ms=20, max_batch_tokens=4096 (2) max_wait_ms=12, add hysteresis to kernel-picker (no switch <256). Compare p50/p95/p99 and cost.
jiang: Also add an experiment metric: kernel_switch_count_per_minute and kv_init_rate. Those were missing from last deploy.
chris: I'll add those to the exporter and push a canary config. Quick config diff:
```yaml
scheduler:
  max_wait_ms: 20    # was 8
  max_batch_tokens: 4096  # was 2048
kernel_picker:
  min_switch_threshold_tokens: 256  # new
metrics:
  emit: [kernel_switch_count,kV_init_rate]
```
maya: For rollout policy: start with 5% for 30m, check p99 and kernel_switch_count. If kernel_switch_count decreases and p99 improves, move to 25%/6h then 100% if stable. Rollback on p99 > baseline +15ms.
olga: Also note: this will slightly increase cost per request if median latency rises for tiny requests. We should include cost delta in the canary dashboard.
jiang: One last thought: we may be able to micro-optimize kernel_switch path to avoid the full handshake when batch shape hasn't changed. But that's more engineering time vs config change trade. For short term, prefer config canary.
maya: Sounds good. @perf-bot please create canary job with those two variants and flag me + chris + olga + jiang.
perf-bot: Created canary run 2026-03-18T09:12Z, variants A/B, 5% initial traffic window ready. /bot will post status. :rocket:
chris: I'll watch exporter metrics and attach a heatmap after first 2 hours.
maya: Thanks team — good plan. We'll reconvene after the 6h check. :thumbsup:
